title: Time: Seconds to Centuries, 24-Hour Time and Time Intervals
seo_title: Grade 5 Time Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Read, tell and write time in 12-hour and 24-hour formats on both analogue and digital instruments in hours, minutes and seconds; use clocks, calendars and stopwatches; calculate time intervals; convert between seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, years, decades and centuries.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 time worksheets: seconds to centuries, 12-hour and 24-hour time, elapsed time and time problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: 60 s = 1 min, 60 min = 1 h, 100 years = 1 century.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 60 seconds = 1 minute, 60 minutes = 1 hour, 24 hours = 1 day.
  • 10 years = 1 decade, 100 years = 1 century, 1 000 years = 1 millennium.
  • 24-hour time: for p.m. times, add 12 to the hour: 4:25 p.m. = 16:25.
  • To find a time interval, count on to the next hour, then the whole hours, then the minutes.

Examples

Example

From 09:45 to 13:20

09:45 → 10:00 is 15 min

10:00 → 13:00 is 3 h

13:00 → 13:20 is 20 min

Answer: 3 hours 35 minutes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
100 seconds1 minute = 60 seconds.
Adding 10 for p.m.Add 12: 7 p.m. = 19:00.
Across noonCount on through 12:00.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 5 say about time?
faq.a: Read, tell and write time in 12-hour and 24-hour formats, use clocks, calendars and stopwatches, calculate time intervals, and convert between seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, years, decades and centuries.

faq.q: How many years is a century?
How do I count an interval?
faq.a: Count on to the next hour first.

items.q: 70 years is how many decades?
items.e: 1 decade = 10 years. 70 ÷ 10 = 7 decades.

items.q: An old church is 1 century, 4 decades and 5 years old. How many years old is it?
A stone bridge is 1 century, 5 decades and 7 years old. How many years old is it?
A baobab tree is 1 century, 1 decade and 9 years old. How many years old is it?
How many years are in 4 centuries?
items.e: 1 century = 100 years, so 4 centuries = 400 years.

items.q: 225 seconds = ☐ minutes ☐ seconds
items.e: 3 × 60 = 180, with 45 seconds left: 3 minutes 45 seconds.

items.q: 5 000 years is how many millennia?
items.e: 1 millennium = 1 000 years. 5 000 ÷ 1 000 = 5 millennia.

items.q: How many years are in 8 centuries?
items.e: 1 century = 100 years, so 8 centuries = 800 years.

items.q: A baobab tree is 3 centuries, 6 decades and 7 years old. How many years old is it?
How many years are in 2 centuries?
items.e: 1 century = 100 years, so 2 centuries = 200 years.

items.q: A stone bridge is 4 centuries, 4 decades and 1 year old. How many years old is it?
800 years is how many centuries?
items.e: 1 century = 100 years. 800 ÷ 100 = 8 centuries.

items.q: How many seconds are in 1 minute?
items.e: There are 60 seconds in 1 minute. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds.)

items.q: How many hours are in 1 day?
items.e: A day is 24 hours: 12 a.m. hours and 12 p.m. hours. 12 + 12 = 24. (Not 12: the hour hand goes around the clock twice in one day.)

items.q: How many days are in a year that is not a leap year?
items.e: A year has 365 days. A leap year has one extra day, February 29, so it has 366. (52 is the number of weeks in a year. 360 uses 30 days in every month, but some months have 31.)

items.q: 4 hours = ? minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 4 × 60 = 240 minutes. (400 counts an hour as 100 minutes. 96 uses 24, but 24 is the hours in a day.)

items.q: 5 minutes = ? seconds
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 5 × 60 = 300 seconds. (500 counts a minute as 100 seconds. 65 adds 60 + 5 instead of multiplying.)

items.q: 3 days = ? hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. 3 × 24 = 72 hours. (36 uses 12 hours in a day. 180 uses 60.)

items.q: 6 weeks = ? days
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 6 × 7 = 42 days. (30 counts only the 5 school days in each week. 13 adds 6 + 7.)

items.q: How many minutes are in three quarters of an hour?
items.e: A quarter of an hour is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes. 3 × 15 = 45 minutes. (75 is three quarters of 100, but an hour is 60 minutes.)

items.q: Write 2:35 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 2 + 12 = 14. So 2:35 pm is 14:35. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 12:35 is 12:35 pm.)

items.q: Write 1:15 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 1 + 12 = 13. So 1:15 pm is 13:15. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 11:15 is 11:15 am.)

items.q: Write 7:55 am in 24-hour time.
items.e: am times are before midday, so the hour stays the same. A 24-hour time always has 4 digits, so put a 0 in front of a 1-digit hour: 7:55 am is 07:55.

items.q: Write 6:25 am in 24-hour time.
items.e: am times are before midday, so the hour stays the same. A 24-hour time always has 4 digits, so put a 0 in front of a 1-digit hour: 6:25 am is 06:25.

items.q: Write 10:50 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 10 + 12 = 22. So 10:50 pm is 22:50.

items.q: Write 8:05 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 8 + 12 = 20. So 8:05 pm is 20:05. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 18:05 is 6:05 pm.)

items.q: Write 10:35 am in 24-hour time.
items.e: am times are before midday, so the hour stays the same. Do not add 12. 10:35 am is 10:35.

items.q: Write 12:05 am in 24-hour time.
items.e: 12 am is the hour just after midnight. In 24-hour time a new day starts at 00:00, so 12:05 am is 00:05.

items.q: Write 3:03 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 3 + 12 = 15. So 3:03 pm is 15:03. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 13:03 is 1:03 pm.)

items.q: Write 6:53 pm in 24-hour time.
items.e: pm times are after midday. Add 12 to the hour: 6 + 12 = 18. So 6:53 pm is 18:53. (Do not just put a 1 in front: 16:53 is 4:53 pm.)

items.q: Write 16:35 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: Hours from 13 to 23 are p.m. times. Take away 12: 16 − 12 = 4. So 16:35 is 4:35 p.m. (Not 6:35 p.m.: do not just drop the 1. 16 − 12 = 4, not 6.)

items.q: Write 9:20 p.m. in 24-hour time.
items.e: p.m. times are after noon. Add 12 to the hour: 9 + 12 = 21. So 9:20 p.m. is 21:20. (09:20 is in the morning.)

items.q: Write 00:45 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: 00 is the hour just after midnight. In 12-hour time that hour is 12 a.m. So 00:45 is 12:45 a.m., 45 minutes after midnight. (12:45 p.m. is 45 minutes after noon.)

items.q: A ferry sails from 09:40 to 11:15. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 09:40 to 10:00 is 20 minutes; 10:00 to 11:00 is 1 hour; 11:00 to 11:15 is 15 minutes. 1 hour + 20 minutes + 15 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes. (Not 1 hour 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A soccer tournament runs from 13:25 to 16:10. How long does it run?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 13:25 to 14:00 is 35 minutes; 14:00 to 16:00 is 2 hours; 16:00 to 16:10 is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 35 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 45 minutes. (Not 2 hours 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A ferry leaves at 14:35. The trip takes 2 hours 50 minutes. What time does it arrive?
items.e: Add 2 hours: 14:35 → 16:35. Then add 50 minutes: 25 minutes takes you to 17:00, and 25 minutes more is 17:25.

items.q: A ferry arrives at 13:10 after a trip of 2 hours 25 minutes. What time did it leave?
items.e: Count back 2 hours: 13:10 → 11:10. Then count back 25 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 11:00, and 15 minutes more is 10:45. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 13:10.)

items.q: A train leaves at 08:35 and arrives at 15:20. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 08:35 to 09:00 is 25 minutes; 09:00 to 15:00 is 6 hours; 15:00 to 15:20 is 20 minutes. 6 hours + 25 minutes + 20 minutes = 6 hours 45 minutes. (Not 6 hours 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A concert starts at 19:40 and lasts 3 hours 35 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 3 hours: 19:40 → 22:40. Then add 35 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 23:00, and 15 minutes more is 23:15.

items.q: An electric bike charges from 18:40 to 21:05. How many minutes is that?
items.e: 18:40 to 19:00 is 20 minutes. 19:00 to 21:00 is 2 hours = 120 minutes. 21:00 to 21:05 is 5 minutes. 20 + 120 + 5 = 145 minutes. (265 subtracts the clock numbers: 2 105 − 1 840 = 265, as if an hour had 100 minutes.)

items.q: Break starts at 10:15 a.m. and ends at 10:32 a.m. How long is break?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour: 32 − 15 = 17 minutes.

items.q: Library time is from 1:05 p.m. to 1:48 p.m. How long is library time?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour: 48 − 5 = 43 minutes.

items.q: Music class is from 9:35 a.m. to 10:20 a.m. How long is music class?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 9:35 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 25 minutes; 10:00 a.m. to 10:20 a.m. is 20 minutes. 25 minutes + 20 minutes = 45 minutes. (Not 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Liam’s swimming lesson is from 4:50 p.m. to 5:35 p.m. How long is the lesson?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 4:50 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 10 minutes; 5:00 p.m. to 5:35 p.m. is 35 minutes. 10 minutes + 35 minutes = 45 minutes. (Not 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Salmon cooks on the barbecue from 5:38 p.m. to 6:21 p.m. How long does it cook?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 5:38 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. is 22 minutes; 6:00 p.m. to 6:21 p.m. is 21 minutes. 22 minutes + 21 minutes = 43 minutes. (Not 83 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Lunch is from 11:48 a.m. to 12:25 p.m. How long is lunch?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon, from a.m. to p.m. Count on in jumps: 11:48 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 12 minutes; 12:00 noon to 12:25 p.m. is 25 minutes. 12 minutes + 25 minutes = 37 minutes. (Not 77 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: The Terry Fox Run at school starts at 10:35 a.m. Elna finishes at 11:22 a.m. How long does she take?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 10:35 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. is 25 minutes; 11:00 a.m. to 11:22 a.m. is 22 minutes. 25 minutes + 22 minutes = 47 minutes. (Not 87 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Lerato’s soccer practice is from 5:45 p.m. to 7:10 p.m. How long is practice?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 5:45 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. is 15 minutes; 6:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 1 hour; 7:00 p.m. to 7:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 1 hour + 15 minutes + 10 minutes = 1 hour 25 minutes. (Not 1 hour 65 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A movie starts at 6:55 p.m. and ends at 9:10 p.m. How long is the movie?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 6:55 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 5 minutes; 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. is 2 hours; 9:00 p.m. to 9:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 5 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 15 minutes. (Not 2 hours 55 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A lacrosse game is from 6:40 p.m. to 8:55 p.m. How long is the game?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 6:40 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 20 minutes; 7:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. is 1 hour; 8:00 p.m. to 8:55 p.m. is 55 minutes. 1 hour + 20 minutes + 55 minutes = 2 hours 15 minutes. (20 minutes + 55 minutes = 75 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes.)

items.q: How long is it from 18:40 to 19:05?
items.e: Count on: 18:40 to 19:00 is 20 minutes, 19:00 to 19:05 is 5 minutes. 20 minutes + 5 minutes = 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 15:50 to 16:05?
items.e: Count on: 15:50 to 16:00 is 10 minutes, 16:00 to 16:05 is 5 minutes. 10 minutes + 5 minutes = 15 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 09:40 to 10:25?
items.e: Count on: 09:40 to 10:00 is 20 minutes, 10:00 to 10:25 is 25 minutes. 20 minutes + 25 minutes = 45 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 15:44 to 16:22?
items.e: Count on: 15:44 to 16:00 is 16 minutes, 16:00 to 16:22 is 22 minutes. 16 minutes + 22 minutes = 38 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 13:39 to 14:26?
items.e: Count on: 13:39 to 14:00 is 21 minutes, 14:00 to 14:26 is 26 minutes. 21 minutes + 26 minutes = 47 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 20:39 to 21:11?
items.e: Count on: 20:39 to 21:00 is 21 minutes, 21:00 to 21:11 is 11 minutes. 21 minutes + 11 minutes = 32 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 16:55 to 19:45?
items.e: Count on: 16:55 to 17:00 is 5 minutes, 17:00 to 19:00 is 2 hours, 19:00 to 19:45 is 45 minutes. 2 hours + 5 minutes + 45 minutes = 2 hours 50 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 10:20 to 13:10?
items.e: Count on: 10:20 to 11:00 is 40 minutes, 11:00 to 13:00 is 2 hours, 13:00 to 13:10 is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 40 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 50 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 14:38 to 18:12?
items.e: Count on: 14:38 to 15:00 is 22 minutes, 15:00 to 18:00 is 3 hours, 18:00 to 18:12 is 12 minutes. 3 hours + 22 minutes + 12 minutes = 3 hours 34 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 09:38 to 12:32?
items.e: Count on: 09:38 to 10:00 is 22 minutes, 10:00 to 12:00 is 2 hours, 12:00 to 12:32 is 32 minutes. 2 hours + 22 minutes + 32 minutes = 2 hours 54 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Break starts at 10:20 a.m. It lasts 25 minutes. What time does break end?
items.e: Add 25 minutes: 10:45 a.m.

items.q: The school bus leaves at 8:35 a.m. The ride takes 40 minutes. What time does it get to school?
items.e: Add 40 minutes: 25 minutes takes you to 9:00 a.m., and 15 minutes more is 9:15 a.m.

items.q: Art class ends at 3:10 p.m. It lasted 35 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 35 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 3:00 p.m., and 25 minutes more is 2:35 p.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 3:10 p.m.)

items.q: Liam starts a science project at 1:45 p.m. and works for 50 minutes. What time does he stop?
items.e: Add 50 minutes: 15 minutes takes you to 2:00 p.m., and 35 minutes more is 2:35 p.m.

items.q: School starts at 8:45 a.m. Elna’s bus ride takes 50 minutes. What time must she get on the bus?
items.e: Count back 50 minutes: 45 minutes takes you to 8:00 a.m., and 5 minutes more is 7:55 a.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 8:45 a.m.)

items.q: Gym class starts at 11:25 a.m. It lasts 55 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 55 minutes: 35 minutes takes you to 12:00 noon, and 20 minutes more is 12:20 p.m. The time goes past 12 noon, so it changes from a.m. to p.m.

items.q: Lunch is ready at 12:15 p.m. The soup cooked for 40 minutes. What time did it start cooking?
items.e: Count back 40 minutes: 15 minutes takes you to 12:00 noon, and 25 minutes more is 11:35 a.m. Counting back past 12 noon changes p.m. to a.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 12:15 p.m.)

items.q: A movie starts at 6:50 p.m. It lasts 1 hour 35 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 6:50 p.m. → 7:50 p.m. Then add 35 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 8:00 p.m., and 25 minutes more is 8:25 p.m.

items.q: It is 10:38 p.m. How long is it until 12:00 midnight?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 10:38 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. is 22 minutes; 11:00 p.m. to 12:00 midnight is 1 hour. 1 hour + 22 minutes = 1 hour 22 minutes. (Not 1 hour 62 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A field trip to Stanley Park starts at 9:40 a.m. It lasts 2 hours 45 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 2 hours: 9:40 a.m. → 11:40 a.m. Then add 45 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 12:00 noon, and 25 minutes more is 12:25 p.m. The time goes past 12 noon, so it changes from a.m. to p.m.

items.q: A concert ends at 9:05 p.m. It lasted 1 hour 50 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 1 hour: 9:05 p.m. → 8:05 p.m. Then count back 50 minutes: 5 minutes takes you to 8:00 p.m., and 45 minutes more is 7:15 p.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 9:05 p.m.)

items.q: Bread rises from 2:20 p.m. for 100 minutes. What time is it ready?
items.e: 100 minutes is not 1 hour: 100 = 60 + 40, so it is 1 hour 40 minutes. Add 1 hour: 2:20 p.m. → 3:20 p.m. Then add 40 minutes: 4:00 p.m. (3:20 p.m. counts 100 minutes as 1 hour.)

items.q: A ringette tournament ends at 4:00 p.m. The last game lasted 135 minutes. What time did the last game start?
items.e: 135 minutes = 60 + 60 + 15 = 2 hours 15 minutes. Count back 2 hours: 4:00 p.m. → 2:00 p.m. Then count back 15 minutes: 1:45 p.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 4:00 p.m.) (2:25 p.m. reads 135 minutes as 1 hour 35 minutes.)

items.q: A salmon pie bakes for 1 hour 10 minutes and then cools for 25 minutes. Dinner is at 6:30 p.m. What is the latest time the pie can go in the oven?
items.e: Add the times first: 1 hour 10 minutes + 25 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes. Count back from 6:30 p.m.: 1 hour → 5:30 p.m. 30 minutes → 5:00 p.m. 5 more minutes → 4:55 p.m. (5:20 p.m. forgets the cooling time. 8:05 p.m. adds instead of counting back.)
The hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The minute hand points to 11: 11 × 5 = 55 minutes past. Times from midnight to midday are am. So it is 8:55 am.
The hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The minute hand points to 4: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes past. Times from midday to midnight are pm. So it is 8:20 pm.
The hour hand is between 6 and 7, so the hour is still 6. The minute hand points to 5: 5 × 5 = 25 minutes past. Times from midday to midnight are pm. So it is 6:25 pm.
The hour hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. The minute hand points to 5: 5 × 5 = 25 minutes past. Times from midnight to midday are am. So it is 9:25 am.
The hour hand is between 3 and 4, so the hour is still 3. The minute hand points to 5: 5 × 5 = 25 minutes past. Times from midday to midnight are pm. So it is 3:25 pm.

The hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is still 5. The minute hand is 2 small marks past the 9. Count in 5s to 45, then on in 1s: 47 minutes past. Times from midday to midnight are pm. So it is 5:47 pm.

items.q: The ferry leaves Swartz Bay at 13:00. What time does it arrive in Tsawwassen?
items.e: Find 13:00 in the “Leaves Swartz Bay” column. Look across that row: it arrives at 14:35. (12:35 and 16:35 are on other rows.)

items.q: How long does the ferry take to go from Swartz Bay to Tsawwassen?
items.e: Take any row, such as 13:00 to 14:35. Count on in jumps: 13:00 to 14:00 is 1 hour; 14:00 to 14:35 is 35 minutes. 1 hour + 35 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes.

items.q: How long does the train take from Waterfront to Metrotown?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 08:47 to 09:00 is 13 minutes; 09:00 to 09:04 is 4 minutes. 13 minutes + 4 minutes = 17 minutes. (Not 57 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Liam arrives in Tsawwassen at 6:35 p.m. Which sailing did he take from Swartz Bay?
items.e: 6:35 p.m. in 24-hour time is 6 + 12 = 18, so 18:35. Find 18:35 in the “Arrives” column. That ferry leaves Swartz Bay at 17:00. (Not 15:00: that ferry arrives at 16:35, which is 4:35 p.m.)

items.q: How long is the whole ride, from Waterfront to King Pieter?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 08:47 to 09:00 is 13 minutes; 09:00 to 09:26 is 26 minutes. 13 minutes + 26 minutes = 39 minutes. (Not 79 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Elna’s family must be in Tsawwassen by 4:00 p.m. What is the latest ferry they can take from Swartz Bay?
items.e: 4:00 p.m. is 16:00. Look down the “Arrives” column for the last time before 16:00: 14:35. That ferry leaves at 13:00. (The 15:00 ferry arrives at 16:35, too late. 14:35 is an arrival time, not a sailing.)

items.q: How long does the train take from Commercial–Broadway to New Westminster?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 08:56 to 09:00 is 4 minutes; 09:00 to 09:11 is 11 minutes. 4 minutes + 11 minutes = 15 minutes. (Not 55 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Ethan gets to the Swartz Bay terminal at 10:05, just after the 09:00 ferry has left. How long must he wait for the next ferry?
items.e: Count on: 10:05 to 11:00 is 55 minutes. So it is 55 minutes. (Not 95 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Ayanda’s swim practice is 1 hour 25 minutes. Lungile’s swim practice is 95 minutes. Whose practice is longer, and by how much?
items.e: 1 hour 25 minutes = 60 + 25 = 85 minutes. 95 − 85 = 10. So Lungile’s practice is longer, by 10 minutes. (Ayanda’s by 30 minutes counts an hour as 100 minutes: 125 − 95 = 30.)

items.q: Chloe gets off at King Pieter and walks 12 minutes to a swim meet that starts at 09:45. How many minutes early is she?
items.e: The train gets to King Pieter at 09:26. 09:26 + 12 minutes = 09:38. 09:38 to 09:45 is 7 minutes. (19 minutes forgets the walk. 31 minutes adds the walk instead of taking it away.)

items.q: A train leaves Central at 16:56. What time does it get to Parramatta?
items.e: Find 16:56 in the Central row. Go down that column to the Parramatta row: 17:24.

items.q: A train gets to Strathfield at 17:41. What time did it leave Central?
items.e: Find 17:41 in the Strathfield row. Go up that column to the Central row: 17:26.

items.q: How long does the train that leaves Central at 16:41 take to get to Parramatta?
items.e: Count on: 16:41 to 17:00 is 19 minutes, 17:00 to 17:09 is 9 minutes. 19 minutes + 9 minutes = 28 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Pieter must be at Parramatta by 17:30. What is the latest train he can catch from Redfern?
items.e: Look along the Parramatta row for the last time that is not after 17:30: 17:24. Go up that column to Redfern: 16:59. The next train gets to Parramatta at 17:39, which is too late.

items.q: Ofentse gets to Redfern at 17:08, just after a train has left. How long must she wait for the next one?
items.e: The 16:59 train has gone. The next train from Redfern is at 17:14. Count on: 17:08 to 17:14 is 6 minutes. So it is 6 minutes.

items.q: Dumisani’s train gets to Strathfield at 4:56 pm. Which time on the timetable is this?
items.e: 4:56 pm is after midday, so add 12 to the hour: 4 + 12 = 16. Look for 16:56 in the Strathfield row.

items.q: The swimming gala starts at 9:35 am and finishes at 14:20. How long does it last?
items.e: Change 9:35 am to 09:35. Count on: 09:35 to 10:00 is 25 minutes, 10:00 to 14:00 is 4 hours, 14:00 to 14:20 is 20 minutes. 4 hours + 25 minutes + 20 minutes = 4 hours 45 minutes. (14:20 is 2:20 pm, not 4:20 pm.)

items.q: Kabelo gets to the pool at 5:10 pm. The sign says the pool closes at 17:45. How long can he swim?
Dinner is at 18:30. A roast takes 1 hour 45 minutes to cook. What time must it go in the oven?
items.e: Count back 1 hour: 18:30 − 1 hour = 17:30. Then count back 45 minutes: 30 minutes to 17:00, then 15 more: 16:45.

items.q: The movie runs until the late news starts. How long is the movie?
items.e: Count on: 20:45 to 21:00 is 15 minutes, 21:00 to 23:00 is 2 hours, 23:00 to 23:10 is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 15 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)
